спавна и слоты игроков. Корабли и прочее — через хук `@sc.pydcs`, без символов для логики.

**Движок:**

* не больше 2 групп и 24 юнитов спавна в секунду;
* задачу только что созданной группе движок отдаёт не раньше чем через 2 кадра и 0,5 с;
* логику, которая перестала читать поток (например, остановлена в отладчике), движок отключает
  после 4096 непрочитанных сообщений; перезапуск подключает её снова;
* подписчик событий, отставший больше чем на 1024 события, пропускает самые старые.

<!-- source: docs/changelog.md -->

# Что нового

Полная история изменений — в
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md) репозитория
SDK.

## 0.1.0

Первый выпуск SDK для авторов миссий.

* Крейт `sortie`: функция миссии `#[sortie::mission]`, программа `sortie::main!`, контекст
  `Ctx`, команды с ключами идемпотентности, ожидание по времени и состоянию мира, события, меню
  F10, флаги, спавн из шаблонов, задачи авиации, состояние сессии, хода и кампании, итоги
  сессии, ошибки с местом в коде.
* Крейт `sortie-build`: символы сценария из `scenario.lock.json` для `build.rs`.
* Генератор `sortie-gen`: сценарий на pydcs, воспроизводимая сборка `.miz` и manifest, lock,
  правило аэродрома игроков, проверка типов через запущенную DCS, регистрация, запуск,
  перезапуск, события и итоги, миссия-заглушка `lobby`, разбор миссий `adopt`.
* Шаблон миссии и пример `op_north`.
* Рантайм 0.1.0: `sortied`, `sortie` (`install`, `doctor`, `status`, `events`,
  `top`) и мост для DCS 2.9.31.

Тесты без DCS появятся в SDK 0.2.

<!-- source: agents/AGENTS.md -->

# Agent instructions: a Sortie mission repository

This repository is one DCS World mission built on the Sortie SDK 0.1.0
(`https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk`, tag `v0.1.0`). It has two halves:

- `scenario.py`: the static mission in Python (sortie-gen over pydcs). It builds the `.miz`,
  its manifest and `scenario.lock.json`, the list of symbols the logic may use.
- the Rust crate: the mission logic, a separate process that attaches to the Sortie engine
  `sortied` running next to DCS. It reads a replica of the DCS world and sends commands.

The SDK is new: its API is not in your training data. Read the matching skill (below) before
you change code, and take every name from it or from the SDK source.

## Layout

```text
Cargo.toml, build.rs     the logic crate; build.rs turns scenario.lock.json into typed symbols
src/lib.rs               sortie::include_scenario!(..) and the #[sortie::mission] function
src/main.rs              sortie::main!(<crate>::run);
scenario.py              the scenario; `ident=` makes a symbol for the logic
scenario.lock.json       generated by `scenario.py lock`; committed, never edited by hand
pyproject.toml           uv project with the sortie-gen dependency
dist/                    offline builds (not committed)
```

## Commands

```powershell
uv sync                                       # Python environment with sortie-gen
uv run python scenario.py lock                # after adding, renaming or removing an ident
uv run python scenario.py build               # offline build into dist/ (no engine needed)
cargo build --release                         # the logic (build.rs reads scenario.lock.json)
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test                                    # plain unit tests only (see Rules)
uv run python scenario.py lock --check        # CI: fails if the lock is stale
```

In DCS (the Sortie runtime installed with `sortie install`, DCS restarted afterwards):

```powershell
sortied --dev                                 # the engine; no token needed locally
uv run python scenario.py register            # a new build (= a new turn) for the engine
cargo run --release -- --dev                  # the logic; attaches and waits for the mission
uv run python scenario.py watch               # live events; `results` after the session
```

## Rules

1. **Symbols come from the scenario.** A new group, zone, template, flag, airbase or menu for
   the logic: add it with `ident=` in `scenario.py`, run `lock`, then `cargo build`. A logic
   built from another lock is refused by the running mission.
2. **Key commands by step.** `spawn_group` and `destroy` always get `.key("step-name")` (they
   are refused without one under `--dev`); so does any command a replay must not repeat. A key
   is stable across runs (a literal or a deterministic counter) and belongs to one command.
3. **The mission function replays.** After a restart of the logic process it runs again from
   the top in the same session. Wait on world state (`ctx.wait_until`), delay with named
   timers (`ctx.timer`), run one-time steps in `ctx.once` and campaign changes in
   `ctx.once_per_turn`.
4. **One thread, short borrows.** No blocking calls; background work through `ctx.spawn`;
   `ctx.world()` and `StateDoc::get()` are dropped before the next `.await`.
5. **No tests without DCS in SDK 0.1.0.** FakeDcs and `#[sortie::test]` arrive in
   SDK 0.2 (`#[sortie::test]` is a compile error until then). Unit-test plain functions with
   `#[test]`; test the mission in DCS with `sortied --dev`.
6. **The `.miz` comes from `scenario.py`.** Change groups, units and zones there, not in the
   Mission Editor. A DO SCRIPT added in a `@sc.pydcs` hook uses
   `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`; a built `.miz` is never loaded and saved again with pydcs.
7. **Multiplayer slots:** a player flight starts at an airfield of its own coalition
   (`player_flight` sets the owner; a hook that adds client groups must do it too).

## Docs and skills

- Skills, one per task: `sortie-mission-logic` (the Rust logic), `sortie-scenario`
  (`scenario.py` and its commands), `sortie-live-debugging` (install, logs, failures in DCS).
  They are in the `agents/` folder of the SDK repository and in
  [the skills zip](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-agent-skills-0.1.0.zip); online:
  [mission logic](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.html),
  [scenario](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-scenario/SKILL.html),
  [live debugging](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-live-debugging/SKILL.html).
- Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/. For agents: [llms.txt](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms.txt) (an index)
  and [llms-full.txt](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms-full.txt) (all docs and skills in one file).
- The SDK source at the tag: `crates/sortie` (the API), `examples/op_north` (a complete
  mission), `python/sortie-gen` (the generator).

# Sortie for AI coding agents

This folder helps coding agents work on a Sortie mission (Sortie SDK 0.1.0). It is
written in English; the SDK docs are in Russian.

| File | For | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [sortie-mission-logic/](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.md) | Claude Code | skill: the mission logic in Rust (`Ctx`, keys, waits, events, menus, state, long multiplayer missions, errors) |
| [sortie-scenario/](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-scenario/SKILL.md) | Claude Code | skill: `scenario.py` with sortie-gen and its commands |
| [sortie-live-debugging/](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-live-debugging/SKILL.md) | Claude Code | skill: install, logs and failures in a live DCS |
| [AGENTS.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/AGENTS.md) | Codex, Cursor, others | instructions for the root of a mission repository |
| [llms.txt](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms.txt) | any agent that reads the web | an index of the docs and skills ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) format) |

The site build packs this whole folder into a zip:
[sortie-agent-skills-0.1.0.zip](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-agent-skills-0.1.0.zip).
Its root holds the three skill folders, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt` and this file.

## Claude Code

A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md`. Claude Code loads skills from `.claude/skills/` of the
project and from `~/.claude/skills/` of the user, and picks a skill by its description when the
task fits (writing logic, editing `scenario.py`, a failure in DCS).

Below, `<skills>` is the unzipped zip or the `agents` folder of the SDK repository.

Into one mission repository (commit them with it, so everyone working on it gets them):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .claude\skills | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Recurse -Force <skills>\sortie-* .claude\skills\
```

For every project of this user:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$HOME\.claude\skills" | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Recurse -Force <skills>\sortie-* "$HOME\.claude\skills\"
```

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -r <skills>/sortie-* .claude/skills/
```

Copy `AGENTS.md` to the repository root too, and add a `CLAUDE.md` with the line
`@AGENTS.md` so Claude Code reads it. After an SDK update, replace the folders with the new
version's.

## Codex, Cursor and other agents

- Put `AGENTS.md` at the root of the mission repository. Codex and Cursor read it there; for
  other tools, point their rules file at it.
- Give an agent that reads the web the index [https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms.txt](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms.txt),
  or the whole text in one file:
  [https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms-full.txt](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/llms-full.txt).
- The skills are plain Markdown: an agent without skill support can read
  `agents/<skill>/SKILL.md` and its `references/` when the task matches the skill's
  `description`.

## How the examples are checked

Every Rust and Python example in these files is compiled: they come from the `frontline`
example scenario (`snippets/python/skills_scenario.py`) and the code in `snippets/src/skills/`
of the SDK repository.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-live-debugging/SKILL.md -->

Skill `sortie-live-debugging` (sortie-live-debugging/SKILL.md): Sortie in a live DCS World: install and `sortie doctor`, `sortied --dev`, attaching the mission and the logic, reading dcs.log, the sortied log, sortie-bridge.log and the logic's stderr. Use when a Sortie mission does not attach or misbehaves in DCS, when the DCS screen shows a "Sortie ..." message, after installing or updating Sortie or DCS, when players cannot take multiplayer slots, after a Mission Editor round trip, or when an error mentions the bridge, the engine, a session or a token.


# Debugging Sortie in a live DCS

The chain, top to bottom; a problem is the first link that is down:

```text
DCS (mission and hooks environments)
  └─ bridge DLL + Lua layer    loaded by one line in <DCS>\Scripts\MissionScripting.lua
                               and by Saved Games\DCS\Scripts\Hooks\sortie-hook.lua
       └─ link (named pipe) ─► sortied (gRPC 127.0.0.1:50777)
                                 ◄─ your logic binary (Logic.Attach)
                                 ◄─ sortie-gen (register, launch, watch, results)
                                 ◄─ sortie CLI (status, events, top)
```

The Saved Games folder is `%USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\DCS` (a dedicated server started with
`-w DCS.server`: `DCS.server`, and every command gets `--instance server`).

## Setup on a machine with DCS

1. Unzip `sortie-runtime-0.1.0-win64.zip` from the GitHub release of
   `lynxr/sortie-sdk` and follow its README; check it against `SHA256SUMS`.
2. `sortie.exe install` from a console **run as administrator**: it copies the Lua layer, the
   hook and the bridge DLL into Saved Games, creates `Sortie\link.secret` and
   `Sortie\tokens.toml`, and adds one line to `<DCS>\Scripts\MissionScripting.lua` (the only
   change in the DCS folder). `--dry-run` shows the plan; `--no-patch` leaves
   `MissionScripting.lua` alone; `--dcs <folder>` picks the install.
3. **Restart DCS itself** (not only the mission). The hooks part of the layer and a new bridge
   DLL load only when DCS starts.
4. `sortie.exe doctor`: done when it exits 0. `doctor --fix` (administrator) restores the
   `MissionScripting.lua` line after a DCS update overwrote it.
5. `sortied.exe --dev`: local API calls need no token; spawns and destroys need `.key()`. Keep
   the console open: it logs every attach and refusal. DCS and `sortied` start in any order.
6. Register the mission (`uv run python scenario.py register`), start the logic
   (`cargo run --release -- --dev`), then fly: open
   `Saved Games\DCS\Missions\Sortie\<scenario>-<build_id>.miz` (single player) or
   `scenario.py launch` (dedicated server).
7. Done when `sortie status` shows `session <id> (<scenario>)` with `1 logic client(s)` and the
   logic's stderr says `session started`.

## Where to look

| Source | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| the DCS screen | `Sortie bridge is not installed: run sortie doctor` (the mission found no bridge); `Sortie: <reason>` (the engine refused the mission) |
| `sortie status` | engine and bridge versions, DCS version, `link hooks/mission: up/down`, the session, model time, `PAUSED`, logic clients, `note` lines with the reason something is degraded |
| `sortie events --kind dead --limit 20`, `scenario.py watch` | the live event stream |
| `sortie top` | health, links, credits, queues, refreshed every second |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Logs\dcs.log` | Lua layer lines start with `Sortie:` (mission) or come from the `SORTIE` subsystem (hooks): link up/down, boot errors. `Select-String Sortie dcs.log` |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Logs\sortie-bridge.log` | the bridge DLL |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Sortie\Logs\sortied.log.*` | the engine (also on its console), including the `doctor` checks it runs at start |
| the logic's stderr | attach, `session started` / `session ended`, every recorded error with its Rust call site; `SORTIE_LOG=debug` for more |
| `scenario.py results` | the outcome, fates, kills, flags and report of the last session |

## The development loop

- **Logic change:** stop the logic (Ctrl-C), `cargo build --release`, start it again. The
  running session continues; the mission function starts with `Start::AfterCrash` and replays:
  keyed commands, `once` and named timers do not repeat. (`sortie dev` with hot reload is not
  available yet.)
- **Scenario change without new symbols** (positions, units, weather): `register` a new
  build and load it. A new build is a new turn: `Start::Fresh`.
- **New or renamed symbols:** `lock`, rebuild the logic, `register`, load the new build. An
  old logic is refused by a mission that lacks its symbols.
- **Same build again:** `scenario.py restart` (multiplayer host or server), or load the same
  `.miz` again in single player: `Start::Restart`, the world is back to the manifest.
- Only one logic per scenario can be attached: stop the old process before starting a new
  one.

## Facts that cause most surprises

- **Restart DCS after `sortie install`.** A new DLL is named in `Scripts\Sortie\pending.txt`
  and becomes active at the next DCS start; the hooks Lua loads only at DCS start. A stale
  layer shows as a `sortie status` note: "the Lua layer DCS loaded differs from what
  `sortie install` put there ...: run `sortie install` again and restart DCS itself".
- **Multiplayer slots and airfields.** DCS offers a parking slot only to the coalition that
  owns the airfield. A player who stays a spectator after picking a slot: the airfield belongs
  to someone else. `player_flight` handles it; a client group added in a `@sc.pydcs` hook needs
  its airfield owner set in the hook (the build warns).
- **Unit ids are strings in DCS 2.9.31.** `Unit:getID()` returns a string there. The Lua layer
  and the engine of this runtime accept both forms; in the SDK `Entity.unit_id` is a number.
  A world that stays empty (no units in `wait_until`, nothing in `sortie events`) with an older
  runtime: install this one and restart DCS.
- **Mission Editor round trips are safe** for a built `.miz` (open, re-save, fly from the
  editor): the bootstrap is an inline DO SCRIPT. The `dcs.log` error
  `[string "DictKey_..."]:1: '=' expected near '<eof>'` means a DO SCRIPT in the dictionary
  form: the `.miz` went through a pydcs load and save, or a hook used pydcs's `DoScript`
  instead of `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`. Groups, units and zones edited in the editor no
  longer match the manifest: edit `scenario.py`.
- **Pause stops model time.** Commands to the mission wait while DCS is paused (unless sent
  with `.on_pause(Fail)`), `ctx.sleep` and timers stop, and the type check of `register` cannot
  run.
- **Measurements of DCS itself** (event ids, timer cadence, sampling cost) are not part of SDK
  0.1.0: `sortie probe` prints "`sortie probe` lands in M0" and exits with code 2;
  `sortie dev`, `sortie trace` and `sortie record` are not built yet either (M4). Report what
  you measure with the DCS version, FPS and hardware.

Failure signatures and fixes, symptom first: [references/failures.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-live-debugging/references/failures.md).
Mission-side errors (`sortie::*` codes): the sortie-mission-logic skill,
`references/errors.md`. Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-live-debugging/references/failures.md -->

# Failure signatures (for agents)

Symptom first. Check the links of the chain in this order: DCS screen and `dcs.log`, then
`sortie status`, then the `sortied` console, then the logic's stderr.

## The mission does not attach

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| screen: `Sortie bridge is not installed: run sortie doctor` | the mission found no `SORTIE` global: the `MissionScripting.lua` line is missing (a DCS update rewrites the file) or the Lua boot failed | `sortie doctor`; `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator; then read the `Sortie:` error in `dcs.log` |
| `dcs.log`: ``Sortie: lfs/io/package are not available: the Sortie line must come before the sanitizer in MissionScripting.lua (run `sortie doctor --fix`)`` | the line sits after the sanitizer | `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator |
| `dcs.log`: ``Sortie: Scripts/Sortie/active.txt is missing: run `sortie install` `` | no bridge installed in this Saved Games folder (or another instance) | `sortie install` with the right `--instance`, restart DCS |
| screen: ``Sortie: build <id> (<scenario>) is not registered with this engine; register it with `sortie-gen register` ...`` | the `.miz` came from an offline `build`, or the engine's database is another one (`--db memory` forgets on restart) | `scenario.py register` and open the registered copy from `Missions\Sortie`, or start `sortied --manifest dist\<id>.manifest.pb` |
| screen: `Sortie: the mission's digest ... does not match build ...` | the `.miz` was changed after the build or belongs to another build | build and register again; edit `scenario.py`, not the `.miz` |
| screen: `Sortie: the mission says scenario ...` / `... schema ...` | the bootstrap and the registered build disagree | rebuild and register |
| nothing on screen; `sortie status`: `link mission: down`, note `no mission link: no Sortie mission is running` | `sortied` is not running, the mission has not started, or the link points elsewhere | start `sortied`; same `--instance` for `install`, `doctor` and `sortied`; `dcs.log`: `mission link down: <error>; retrying` names the reason |
| note `the DCS hooks link is not connected (is DCS running with Scripts/Hooks/sortie-hook.lua?)` | DCS was not restarted after the install, or the hook is missing | restart DCS; `sortie doctor` checks `hook` |
| note ``the Lua layer DCS loaded differs from what `sortie install` put there (...): run `sortie install` again and restart DCS itself`` | an update of the layer while DCS ran | as it says (for the mission part: restart the mission) |
| `dcs.log`: ``[string "DictKey_..."]:1: '=' expected near '<eof>'`` | a DO SCRIPT in pydcs's dictionary form | rebuild from `scenario.py`; hooks use `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`; never load/save a built `.miz` with pydcs |

## The logic does not run

| Symptom (logic stderr) | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ``cannot reach the engine at http://127.0.0.1:50777: ... (is `sortied` running?); retrying in N s`` | no engine at that address | start `sortied`; `--engine` / `SORTIE_ENGINE` |
| `attaching`, then nothing | no session of this scenario runs yet; the logic waits for one | start the mission; the scenario name of the logic and the mission must match |
| ``error[sortie::transport]: Logic.Attach at ... failed: ... (set SORTIE_TOKEN to a token with the `logic` role)``, exit code 2 | `sortied` without `--dev` needs a token | `SORTIE_TOKEN` from `Saved Games\DCS\Sortie\tokens.toml` (role `logic`), or `sortied --dev` on your own machine |
| ``error[sortie::rejected]: the engine rejected this logic: logic `x` was built against a different `s` schema: N symbol(s) missing from the running mission``, exit code 2 | the mission in DCS lacks symbols the logic was built with | build the logic and the mission from the same `scenario.lock.json`; `register` and load the new build |
| ``another PRIMARY logic is attached for `s` `` | a second copy of the logic | stop the old process |
| `the engine shut this logic down`, exit code 0 | the engine stopped, or the logic stopped reading (a blocked thread: 4096 unread messages) | restart it; remove the blocking code |
| `session started` with `kind=AfterCrash` after a restart of the logic | expected: same session, the mission function replays | nothing; keys, `once` and timers keep it from repeating |

## The mission runs, but wrong

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a player picks a slot and stays a spectator (multiplayer) | the airfield belongs to another coalition | `player_flight` sets the owner; for a client group from a hook, set the airfield's coalition in the hook; read the build warnings |
| `sortie status` shows the session, but `wait_until` on units never fires and `sortie events` stays silent | the world stays empty: an older runtime reads DCS 2.9.31's string unit ids as numbers | install the current runtime, restart DCS |
| `sortie::invalid`: spawn or destroy without a key | `sortied --dev` or the logic's `--dev` | `.key("step-name")` |
| a spawn twice after a logic restart | the spawn had no key, or its key changes between runs | a stable key per step |
| `sortie::timeout` on spawns, note `N command(s) waiting: spawn rate limit (2 groups / 24 units per second)` | too many spawns at once | spawn in a loop, cap the count, raise `.timeout(..)` |
| commands hang, `sortie status` says `PAUSED` | DCS is paused: mission commands wait | unpause, or `.on_pause(v1::PausePolicy::Fail)` |
| `ctx.group(groups::X)` → `sortie::not_in_world` | late activation or the group is dead | spawn it from a template instead; check `alive_count()` |
| `ctx.group(groups::X)` → `sortie::unknown_symbol` | the mission in DCS was built from another lock | rebuild both sides from one lock |
| `register` stops: `DCS on the server does not know N type(s) ...` | a misspelled type or a module or mod missing on the server | fix the type or install it there; `--no-validate` skips |
| `register` warns `unit and static types not checked: ...` | no mission ran in DCS, or it was paused | run the lobby (`sortie-gen lobby`) unpaused |
| `scenario.py restart` → `FAILED_PRECONDITION`: `Missions.Restart needs DCS running as a multiplayer server ...` | single player | restart from the DCS menu, or host in multiplayer |
| `restart` → `DCS did not say whether it runs multiplayer: the Sortie hooks layer DCS loaded predates ...` | DCS was not restarted after `sortie install` | restart DCS itself |
| `scenario.py launch` fails on a single-player DCS | `launch` loads missions through the server API | open the registered `.miz` yourself |

## `sortie doctor` checks

| Check | When it fails | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dcs install`, `saved games`, `writedir` | wrong folder or instance | `--dcs <DCS World folder>`, `--instance <name>`, `--saved-games <folder>` |
| `MissionScripting`, `sanitizer` | the line is missing, misplaced, or the sanitizer was changed | `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator; restore the stock sanitizer |
| `hook`, `lua layer`, `bridge dll` | files missing or changed | `sortie install`, then restart DCS |
| `lua.dll` | this DCS build changed `lua.dll`: the bridge does not match it | a runtime release built for this DCS version is needed: report it |
| `link secret`, `api tokens` | not created yet | `sortie install` |
| `missionList` | an empty mission list on a dedicated server (the server does not start) | add a mission, e.g. a `sortie-gen lobby` mission |
| `unsafe api` (warning) | `autoexec.cfg` opens `net.allow_unsafe_api` to missions | Sortie does not need it |

<!-- source: agents/sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.md -->

Skill `sortie-mission-logic` (sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.md): Sortie mission logic in Rust (crate `sortie`, DCS World). Use when writing or changing a `#[sortie::mission]` or code that uses `Ctx` (commands, `.key()`, `ctx.once`, waits, events, F10 menus, flags, state, timers, `end_session`), when handling `Start` kinds, when a `sortie::*` error code appears (`sortie::gone`, `sortie::invalid`, `sortie::unknown_symbol`, ...), or when designing a long multiplayer mission. Applies to any crate that depends on `sortie` or calls `sortie::include_scenario!`.


# Sortie mission logic

The mission logic is an ordinary async Rust program next to DCS. The engine `sortied` owns
the link to DCS; the logic attaches to it over gRPC and gets one call of its mission function
per session.

- **Reads are local and synchronous.** `ctx.world()` is a replica of the DCS world, updated
  10 times a second and by every event. No RPC.
- **Writes are commands.** Every write is a `Cmd` builder; `.await` sends it and resolves when
  DCS has executed it (or with a `sortie::Error`).
- **The mission function is a replayable script.** It runs again from the top when the logic
  process restarts inside a running session (`Start::AfterCrash`). Every step must be safe to
  run twice: keyed commands, `ctx.once`, named timers, waits on world state.
- **One thread.** `Ctx` is cheap to clone and not `Send`; background work is `ctx.spawn`.
- **Typed scenario.** `groups::X`, `zones::X`, `templates::X`, `flags::X`, `airbases::X`,
  `menus::X` come from the scenario lock; a symbol of another scenario does not compile.

## Project layout

A mission repository starts as a copy of the SDK's `template/` folder:

```text
my-mission/
  Cargo.toml             # the logic crate (package my_mission_logic)
  build.rs               # turns the lock into typed symbols
  src/lib.rs             # include_scenario! and the #[sortie::mission]
  src/main.rs            # one line: sortie::main!(my_mission_logic::run);
  scenario.py            # the scenario (sortie-gen); see the sortie-scenario skill
  scenario.lock.json     # written by `python scenario.py lock`; commit it, never edit it
  pyproject.toml         # uv project with the sortie-gen dependency
```

`examples/op_north` keeps the crate in a `logic/` subfolder instead; both work.

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "my_mission_logic"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"

[dependencies]
sortie = { git = "https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk", tag = "v0.1.0" }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }   # only for state documents

[build-dependencies]
sortie-build = { git = "https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk", tag = "v0.1.0" }

[lints.clippy]
await_holding_refcell_ref = "deny"   # catches a world borrow held across .await
```

- `build.rs`: `fn main() { sortie_build::scenario("my_mission", "scenario.lock.json").emit(); }`.
  The first argument is the scenario name; the path is relative to the crate's `Cargo.toml`.
- `src/lib.rs` starts with `sortie::include_scenario!(my_mission);`, which defines
  `pub mod my_mission` with the marker type `MyMission` and the symbol modules.
- `src/main.rs` is `sortie::main!(my_mission_logic::run);`: arguments, attach, reconnects.
- A private SDK repository needs credentials for cargo (`net.git-fetch-with-cli = true` in
  `.cargo/config.toml`, plus your git credential helper) and for uv: see the docs.

## The mission function

The examples in this skill use the `frontline` scenario of the sortie-scenario skill.

```rust
use sortie::prelude::*;

// lib.rs of the logic crate also has `sortie::include_scenario!(frontline);`
use frontline::{Frontline, groups, zones};

#[sortie::mission] // runs once per session of `frontline`
pub async fn run(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let sam = ctx.group(groups::SAM_NORTH)?; // Group<Ground>, checked against the manifest
    sam.set_option(Alarm::Green).key("sam-dark").await?;

    if start.is_fresh() {
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text("SAM North is cold. Push when ready.")
            .secs(20)
            .key("intro")
            .await?;
    }

    // Evaluated on the local replica after every tick and every event: no RPC.
    ctx.wait_until(|w| {
        w.units()
            .coalition(Coalition::Blue)
            .air()
            .any_inside(zones::SAM_RING)
    })
    .await;
    sam.set_option(Alarm::Red).key("sam-hot").await?;

    // A state, not an event: still correct when the function runs again after a crash.
    ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&sam).alive_count() == 0).await;
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::BlueWin)
        .text("SAM North is down")
        .await
}
```

`#[sortie::mission]` checks the signature: `async fn`, `ctx: Ctx<M>` first, `start: Start`
second, return type `sortie::Result<()>`. Returning `Err` records a logic error with the call
site; the session goes on.

## Workflow

1. **Symbols first.** Everything the logic names (a group, zone, template, flag, airbase or
   menu) needs an `ident=` in `scenario.py`. Add it there, run `python scenario.py lock`, then
   build the logic. Groups added only by a `@sc.pydcs` hook have no symbol: reach them by DCS
   name in world queries (`w.group("Name")`, `.in_group("Name")`).
2. **Write the step replay-safe** (rules below), then `cargo build` and `cargo clippy`.
   Done when both pass and every `spawn_group` and `destroy` in the diff carries `.key(..)`.
3. **Run it in DCS** with `sortied --dev` and the logic's `--dev` (see the
   sortie-live-debugging skill). SDK 0.1.0 has no tests without DCS: FakeDcs
   arrives in SDK 0.2, and `#[sortie::test]` is a compile error until then. Put pure decisions
   (which wave, which target) in plain functions and test them with ordinary `#[test]`.

## Rules

1. **Key every command whose repetition matters.** `spawn_group` and `destroy` always: they
   are refused without a key when `sortied` runs with `--dev` and when the logic runs with
   `--dev`. Key messages, smoke, flags and menu commands that a replay must not repeat. Key
   semantics:
   - the scope is the session: within it, a key that already ran returns the stored result
     without reaching DCS (a replayed spawn returns the same `Group`);
   - a key names a step, so it is the same on every run: a literal (`"red-cap-1"`) or built
     from a deterministic counter (`format!("wave-{n}")`), never from model time, a random
     number or an Eid;
   - one key, one command: reusing a key for a different body (other text, other target) fails
     with `sortie::invalid` ("key `k` was already used for a different command in session ...");
   - a keyed command that timed out after reaching DCS is not sent again on retry with the
     same key: the retry waits for the late result;
   - a mission restart is a new session: keys start empty again.
2. **Wait on states, not events,** when the condition is visible in the world:
   `ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&sam).alive_count() == 0)`. A replay sees the state; it never
   sees an event that happened before it subscribed.
3. **Delays that must survive a logic restart are named timers:**
   `ctx.timer("cap-delay", mins(10))`. `ctx.sleep` starts over after a restart.
4. **Campaign changes go inside `ctx.once_per_turn`.** After a mission restart the turn is
   played again in a new session; `once_per_turn` keeps a kill from being counted twice in one
   turn. `ctx.once` is per session.
5. **Short borrows.** Take `ctx.world()` and `StateDoc::get()` in a statement or a block that
   ends before the next `.await`. A borrow held across `.await` stops the replica from updating
   (the runtime records "the world replica is borrowed across an `.await`").
6. **Never block the thread.** No `std::thread::sleep`, blocking I/O or long CPU loops: ticks
   stop, and after 4096 unread messages the engine detaches the logic (it exits with code 0).
   Wait with `ctx.sleep`, `ctx.timer`, `ctx.wait_until`.
7. **Background work is `ctx.spawn`.** Its tasks end with the session; an `Err` or a panic in
   one is recorded with its call site and the other tasks keep running. No `std::thread`, no
   runtime of your own.

## Start kinds

```rust
match start {
    // First session of this build: the world is as the manifest describes it.
    Start::Fresh => {}
    // The mission was reloaded (same turn): a fresh world, fresh keys and `once`s;
    // `once_per_turn` and the campaign state remember the earlier session.
    Start::Restart => {
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text("Mission restarted")
            .key("restarted")
            .await?;
    }
    // The logic process restarted inside a running session (crash, or you restarted it
    // after a rebuild): the world is as it is now; keys, `once` and timers remember.
    // `Resumed` (the engine resumed the session after its own restart) is not sent yet;
    // treat it the same way.
    Start::AfterCrash | Start::Resumed => {}
}
```

| `Start` | When | The world | Keys, `once`, timers | `once_per_turn`, campaign state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Fresh` | first session of this build (turn) | as in the manifest | empty | as stored |
| `Restart` | the mission was reloaded (`scenario.py restart`, or the same build loaded again) | as in the manifest | empty (new session) | remembered |
| `AfterCrash` | the logic process restarted in the running session (crash, or restarted after a rebuild) | as it is now | remembered | remembered |
| `Resumed` | the engine resumed a session after its own restart (not sent yet) | as it is now | remembered | remembered |

A replay-safe mission needs no branch on `Start` except for player-facing extras (a briefing on
`Fresh`, a notice on `Restart`).

## API map

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| a scenario group | `ctx.group(groups::X)?` → `Group<Ground/Air/Helo/Ship>`; `set_option(Alarm::Red / Roe::..)`, `destroy()`, `push_task`/`set_task` (air and helicopters) |
| spawn | `ctx.spawn_group(templates::X)` or `templates::X.named("..")`, then `.from_airbase(airbases::Y, StartType::..)` or `.at(Vec3, heading_rad)`, `.key(..)` → `Group<K>` |
| tell players | `ctx.message(Coalition::Blue / &group / press.group / sortie::MessageTarget::All).text(..).secs(..)` |
| read the world | `ctx.world()`, `w.units().coalition(..).air().in_zone(zones::X).count()`, `w.players()`, `w.group(&g).alive_count()` |
| wait | `ctx.wait_until(pred)`, `ctx.timer(name, dur)`, `ctx.sleep(dur)`, `ctx.until_session_end()` |
| react | `ctx.events().of::<v1::Dead>().in_group(&g)`; `use sortie::proto::v1;` |
| F10 menu | `ctx.menu(Coalition::Blue).per_group().command(menus::X).key(..).await?`, then `.presses()` |
| flags | `ctx.flag(flags::X).set(true)`, `.get()` → `i32` |
| remember | `ctx.state::<T>("name")` (campaign), `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Turn, ..)`, `ctx.once`, `ctx.once_per_turn` |
| results | `ctx.report().set("key", value)`, `ctx.end_session(Outcome::BlueWin).text(..)` |

Signatures, defaults and an example for each: [references/api.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/api.md).

## More

- [references/patterns.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/patterns.md): a long multiplayer mission (thousands of
  units, players joining and leaving, AI waves, polling, scores) and the anti-patterns.
- [references/errors.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/errors.md): every `sortie::*` error code, the build and
  attach errors, and their fixes.
- Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/. Scenario side: the sortie-scenario skill. Running in DCS:
  the sortie-live-debugging skill.
