# Sortie SDK API reference (for agents)

Everything below is in `sortie::prelude::*` unless a path is given. Event and state enums live
in `sortie::proto::v1` (`use sortie::proto::v1;`). The examples use the `frontline` scenario
(module `frontline`, marker `Frontline`).

## Commands

Every write returns a `Cmd<..>`. Nothing happens until it is awaited; `.await` gives
`sortie::Result<Output>`.

```rust
ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), SmokeColor::Red)
    .key("smoke-obj")
    .await?;
ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN)
    .set(true)
    .key("flag-sam-down")
    .await?;

let cap = ctx
    .spawn_group(templates::RED_CAP.named("Red CAP 1"))
    .from_airbase(airbases::MAYKOP, StartType::Runway)
    .key("red-cap-1") // spawn and destroy: always keyed
    .await?; // Group<Air>
cap.push_task(
    Task::cap(zones::SAM_RING)
        .altitude(ft(25_000))
        .speed(kts(420)),
)
.timeout(secs(5))
.await?;
cap.set_option(Roe::WeaponFree).await?;

let armor = ctx.group(groups::RED_ARMOR)?;
armor.destroy().key("armor-despawn").await?;
```

Options on every command:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.key(impl Into<String>)` | idempotency key, scope: the session (see the rules in SKILL.md) |
| `.timeout(Duration)` | fail with `sortie::timeout` if DCS has not answered; default 10 s, 30 s for `spawn_group` and `destroy` |
| `.on_pause(v1::PausePolicy::Fail)` | fail with `sortie::paused` instead of waiting while the simulation is paused (default: wait) |
| `.after(&other_cmd)` | run only after `other_cmd` (not yet awaited) completed |
| `.lane(v1::Lane::..)` | scheduling lane; the default fits the command |
| `.id()` | the command id, shown in errors |

| Command | Output | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctx.message(to).text(..).secs(u32).clear_view()` | `()` | `to`: `Coalition`, `&Group<K>`, `AnyGroup` (a menu press), `sortie::MessageTarget::All`; 10 s by default |
| `ctx.smoke(at, SmokeColor::Red)` | `()` | `at`: a `MapPoint` (on the ground) or a `Vec3` |
| `ctx.flag(flags::X).set(v)` / `.get()` | `()` / `i32` | `v`: `bool` or `i32` |
| `ctx.spawn_group(t)` | `Group<K>` | `t`: `templates::X` or `templates::X.named("Name")`; then `.from_airbase(airbases::Y, StartType::{Runway, Hot, Cold, Air})` or `.at(Vec3, heading_rad)`; without either, the template's own placement. Default name `<template name>#<session4>-<n>`, units `<group>-<k>`; `.named` fails with `sortie::name_conflict` if a live group has the name. The engine paces spawns (currently 2 groups or 24 units a second), so a big wave takes time. |
| `group.set_option(o)` | `()` | `o`: `Alarm::{Auto, Green, Red}` or `Roe::{WeaponFree, OpenFireWeaponFree, OpenFire, ReturnFire, WeaponHold}` |
| `group.destroy()` | `()` | despawn; no DEAD event follows (a `UnitGone` does) |
| `group.push_task(task)` / `group.set_task(task)` | `()` | `Group<Air>` and `Group<Helo>` only; push on the task stack or replace it |
| `ctx.menu(c).command(menus::X)` | `MenuCommand<S>` | see Menus |
| `ctx.end_session(outcome).text(..)` | `()` | ends the session (the turn); succeeds even if the session ends first |

Tasks (`Task` is in the prelude):

| Task | Defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Task::cap(zones::X).altitude(Length).speed(Speed)` | 6000 m, 420 kt |
| `Task::orbit(MapPoint).altitude(..).speed(..).race_track(MapPoint)` | 6000 m, 350 kt, a circle without `race_track` |
| `Task::rtb(airbases::X)` | |
| `Task::raw(sortie::proto::LuaValue)` | a DCS task table, not checked |

Units and geometry: `m`, `km`, `ft`, `nm` → `Length`; `kts`, `mps`, `kmh` → `Speed`; `secs`,
`mins`, `hours` → `Duration`. `MapPoint { north, east }` (metres, map axes): `.alt(Length)` →
`Vec3`, `.distance(p)`, `.offset(north_m, east_m)`, `.bearing_to(p)`,
`.toward(bearing_rad, Length)`. `Vec3 { x: north, y: up, z: east }`: `.map_point()`. Zones:
`zones::X.center()`, `zones::X.contains(p)`.

Groups: `ctx.group(groups::X)?` returns the live group or `sortie::not_in_world` (no live unit:
late activation, destroyed) or `sortie::unknown_symbol` (the running mission lacks the symbol).
`Group<K>` is bound to one life of the group: a group respawned under the same name is a new
handle. Methods: `eid()`, `name()`, `alive_count()`, `is_alive()`, `any()` → `AnyGroup`.

## Keys in loops

```rust
for n in 1..=3 {
    ctx.timer(&format!("wave-{n}-delay"), mins(5)).await; // deadline stored in the engine
    let wave = ctx
        .spawn_group(templates::RED_CAP)
        .from_airbase(airbases::MAYKOP, StartType::Hot)
        .key(format!("wave-{n}")) // same n, same key: never spawned twice
        .await?;
    ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&wave).alive_count() == 0).await;
}
```

After a logic restart the loop runs again from `n = 1`: passed timers return at once, keyed
spawns return their stored groups, and the waits on dead groups pass. The script fast-forwards
to where it was.

## Once

`Campaign` here and below is a state document type:
`#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Campaign { pub sams_killed: u32 }`.

```rust
let campaign = ctx.state::<Campaign>("campaign").await?; // campaign scope: kept across turns

// Once per session: skipped when the function runs again after a crash.
ctx.once("briefing", async |ctx| {
    ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
        .text("Destroy SAM North.")
        .secs(30)
        .await
})
.await?;

// Once per turn (= per mission build): also skipped after a mission restart.
ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count() == 0)
    .await;
ctx.once_per_turn("count-sam-kill", async |ctx| {
    campaign.update(|c| c.sams_killed += 1).await?;
    ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN).set(true).await
})
.await?;
```

`ctx.once(name, f)` and `ctx.once_per_turn(name, f)` return `Ok(Some(value))` when `f` ran and
`Ok(None)` when it had run before. The mark is written after `f` succeeded: an `Err` from `f`
leaves it unmarked.

## Waiting

```rust
ctx.sleep(secs(30)).await; // model time; stops while paused; starts over after a crash
ctx.timer("cap-delay", mins(10)).await; // named: the deadline survives a logic restart

let blue_in_front = |w: &World| {
    w.units()
        .coalition(Coalition::Blue)
        .in_zone(zones::FRONT)
        .any()
};
ctx.wait_until(blue_in_front).await;

let red_left = ctx.world().group(&groups::RED_ARMOR).alive_count(); // a short borrow
ctx.report().set("red_armor_left", red_left);

// Any end: the logic, the time limit, a restart. Code after it runs only up to the next
// .await; then the session's tasks are aborted.
let end = ctx.until_session_end().await;
eprintln!("session ended: {:?} ({:?})", end.outcome, end.reason); // the logic's stderr
```

- `wait_until` checks its predicate now, after every tick (10 per second) and after every
  event. Keep the predicate cheap; see patterns.md for thousands of units.
- `sleep`, `timer`: model time; a pause stops them.
- `until_session_end()` → `SessionEnd { outcome: Option<Outcome>, text, reason }`, with
  `sortie::EndReason`: `Logic`, `TimeLimit`, `Restart`, `MissionUnloaded`, `EngineShutdown`,
  `Replaced`, `Disconnected`, `Unspecified`. When the session ends, pending commands fail with
  `sortie::session_ended` (not a logic error) and every task of the session is aborted.
- `ctx.model_time()`, `ctx.paused()`, `ctx.is_session_ended()`, `ctx.session_id()`,
  `ctx.turn()` (the build id of the running mission).

World queries (`ctx.world()` or the `wait_until` argument, a `&World`):

| Query | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `w.units()` (live units) | filters `.coalition(c)`, `.air()`, `.planes()`, `.helos()`, `.ground()`, `.ships()`, `.statics()`, `.any_category()`, `.dead()`, `.including_dead()`, `.players()`, `.in_group(&g)`, `.of_type("F-16C_50")`, `.in_zone(zones::X)`, `.within(point, km(5))`; results `.count()`, `.any()`, `.first()`, `.iter()`, `.eids()`, `.nearest_to(point)`, `.inside(&zone)`, `.any_inside(zone)`, `.count_inside(zone)` |
| `w.players()`, `w.statics()` | the same query, preset |
| `w.group(&g)` | `g`: a `Group<K>`, `&groups::X`, a DCS group name; `.exists()`, `.alive_count()`, `.size()`, `.is_dead()`, `.center()`, `.any_inside(z)`, `.count_inside(z)`, `.all_inside(z)`, `.units()`, `.alive_units()`; a missing group counts as empty |
| `w.airbase_by_ident("MAYKOP")`, `w.airbase_by_name(..)`, `w.airbases()` | airbases with their current owner |

An entity (`&sortie::world::Entity`) has `name`, `type_name`, `coalition`, `category`,
`group_name`, `pos: Option<Vec3>`, `velocity`, `heading`, `player: Option<String>`, `life`,
`dead`.

## Events

```rust
let sam = ctx.group(groups::SAM_NORTH)?;
// Subscribe first, then act: a stream only sees events from the moment it was made.
let mut deaths = ctx.events().of::<v1::Dead>().in_group(&sam);
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    while let Some(dead) = deaths.next().await {
        let name = dead.initiator.map(|u| u.name).unwrap_or_default();
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text(format!("{name} destroyed"))
            .secs(10)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(()) // `None`: the session ended
});
```

- `ctx.events()` → `Events`, `.next().await` → `Option<v1::Event>` (`ev.kind`,
  `ev.model_time`, `ev.seq`); `None` once the session ended.
- `.of::<E>()` keeps one type; filters `.in_group(&g)` (a `Group<K>` matches only its own life;
  a `GroupRef` or a name matches whatever group has it now), `.coalition(c)`, `.filter(|e| ..)`.
  They test the event's subject: the initiator, `unit` for `PlayerEnteredUnit`, `last_known`
  for `UnitGone`.
- Types: `Birth`, `Dead`, `UnitLost`, `Kill`, `Hit` (the initiator may be missing), `Shot`,
  `Takeoff`, `Land`, `BaseCaptured`, `Mark`, `PlayerEnteredUnit` (built from BIRTH and the
  player name: multiplayer clients do not get a reliable DCS event), `UnitGone` (left the world
  without DEAD: despawned, missing from a sample), `MenuPressed`, `PlayerConnected`,
  `PlayerDisconnected`, `PlayerChangedSlot`, `ChatMessage`, `SimulationPaused`,
  `SimulationResumed`, `Gap` (events were lost; the replica was resynced), `Unknown`.
- Each event is applied to the replica before your code sees it: in a `Dead` handler the unit
  already counts as dead.
- A stream sees events from the moment it was created. A stream that falls more than 1024
  events behind skips the oldest and logs a warning.

## Menus

```rust
let smoke = ctx
    .menu(Coalition::Blue)
    .per_group() // every blue player group gets the command; a press carries the group
    .command(menus::SMOKE_OBJECTIVE)
    .key("menu-smoke")
    .await?;
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    let mut presses = smoke.presses();
    while let Some(p) = presses.next().await {
        ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), SmokeColor::Red)
            .await?;
        ctx.message(p.group)
            .text("Red smoke on the objective")
            .secs(10)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
});

let sitrep = ctx
    .menu(Coalition::Blue)
    .command(menus::SITREP)
    .key("menu-sitrep")
    .await?;
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    let mut presses = sitrep.presses();
    while presses.next().await.is_some() {
        let left = ctx.world().group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count();
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text(format!("SAM North: {left} alive"))
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
});
```

- `ctx.menu(coalition)` is one command for the whole coalition; a press is a
  `CoalitionPress { coalition, model_time }`. `.per_group()` installs it for every player group
  of the coalition (those present now and each new one at its first player BIRTH); a press is
  a `GroupPress { group: AnyGroup, coalition, model_time }`, and `ctx.message(p.group)` answers
  that group.
- Label and sub-menu path come from `scenario.py` (`sc.menu(ident, label, path=[..])`).
- Presses are queued from the moment the command is installed. Each press goes to one
  `Presses` stream. `menu.remove()` removes the command. Adding the same command twice changes
  nothing in DCS.

## Flags

```rust
let sam_down = ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN);
sam_down.set(1).key("sam-down").await?; // bool or i32
let value: i32 = sam_down.get().await?; // reads DCS (a mission trigger may change it too)
```

## State and results

```rust
#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Progress {
    waves_sent: u32,
}
// Campaign scope (default): kept across turns; the generator can read it.
let campaign = ctx.state::<Campaign>("campaign").await?;
// Turn scope: survives mission restarts of this build; session scope: this session only.
let turn = ctx
    .state_in::<Progress>(v1::StateScope::Turn, "progress")
    .await?;

turn.update(|p| p.waves_sent += 1).await?; // compare-and-swap, retried on conflict
let killed = campaign.get().sams_killed; // a local copy; do not hold `get()` across .await
ctx.report().set("sams_killed", killed); // MissionResults.report_json, read by `results`
```

| Scope | Lives | API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v1::StateScope::Session` | this session | `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Session, name)` |
| `v1::StateScope::Turn` | this build (turn), across mission restarts | `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Turn, name)` |
| `v1::StateScope::Campaign` | across turns of the scenario | `ctx.state::<T>(name)` |

`T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Default` (`#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]`; the
crate needs `serde` with the `derive` feature). `StateDoc<T>`: `get()` (local copy),
`update(|t| ..)` (compare-and-swap; on a conflict it reloads and applies the closure again, up
to 8 times), `set(value)`, `reload()`, `revision()`. The engine stores the documents (SQLite)
and the generator reads them.

`ctx.report().set(key, value)` writes a key of the session's results (`scenario.py results`);
it does not wait, and a failure shows up as a logic error.

## Binary and environment

`sortie::main!(my_mission_logic::run)` makes the binary:

```text
my_mission_logic [--engine <url>] [--build-id <id>] [--logic <name>] [--dev]
  --engine     engine gRPC address (SORTIE_ENGINE, default http://127.0.0.1:50777)
  --build-id   build id announced to the engine (SORTIE_BUILD_ID, default <binary>@<version>)
  --logic      logic name (default: the binary name)
  --dev        spawns and destroys without .key() fail at the call site (SORTIE_DEV=1)
```

`SORTIE_TOKEN`: the API token (role `logic`; not needed with `sortied --dev`). `SORTIE_LOG`:
the log filter (default `info`; logs go to stderr). `--standby` (hot reload) is not available
yet. The binary reconnects with a backoff of 1 to 30 s. Exit codes: 0 after the engine shut it
down, 2 for bad arguments, a refused token or a rejected attach, 1 if the runtime could not
start.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/errors.md -->

# Sortie errors and fixes (for agents)

A command error is a `sortie::Error` with a stable code and the Rust call site that built the
command:

```text
error[sortie::gone]: `push_task` on group "Red CAP 1": Unit doesn't exist (at logic/src/lib.rs:48:9)
```

`e.report()` is the long form the runtime logs: the call site, the Lua traceback, the session
and command ids and a `help:` line. `e.code()`, `e.origin()`, `e.lua_traceback()`,
`e.failure()` (op, target, message) give the parts; `e.is_session_ended()` tells the normal
end of a session from a failure.

## Handling errors in a mission

```rust
let sam = match ctx.group(groups::SAM_NORTH) {
    Ok(g) => g,
    // In the manifest, but no live unit now (late activation, already destroyed).
    Err(sortie::Error::NotInWorld { .. }) => return Ok(()),
    // UnknownSymbol: the running mission was built from another scenario lock.
    Err(e) => return Err(e),
};
match sam.set_option(Alarm::Red).key("sam-hot").await {
    Ok(()) => {}
    // The group died between the check and the command: expected in a live mission.
    Err(sortie::Error::Gone(f)) => eprintln!("SAM North is gone: {}", f.message),
    // The session ended while the command was in flight: not a logic error.
    Err(e) if e.is_session_ended() => return Ok(()),
    // Anything else: the runtime records it with `e.report()` (code, call site, hint).
    Err(e) => return Err(e),
}
```

An `Err` that leaves the mission function or a task spawned with `ctx.spawn` is recorded as a
logic error (stderr of the logic, with its call site) and ends that task only. `SessionEnded`
is never recorded. A panic is recorded the same way, with its location.

## Command errors

| Code | Meaning | Usual cause → fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sortie::gone` | the target no longer exists in DCS | it died or was despawned before the command ran → match `Error::Gone` where a target can die (always in a live mission) |
| `sortie::timeout` | DCS did not answer in time (10 s, 30 s for spawns and destroys) | a big spawn wave queued behind the spawn pacing, or a busy server → `.timeout(..)`, spawn in smaller steps, check `sortie status` / `sortie top` |
| `sortie::lua_error` | the Lua layer raised an error | a bad `Task::raw` table, a wrong option for the unit type → read `e.lua_traceback()` |
| `sortie::invalid` | the command does not fit | a spawn or destroy without `.key(..)` under `--dev`; a key reused for another command ("key `k` was already used for a different command in session ..."); a manifest without the template |
| `sortie::name_conflict` | a live group already has this name | `.named("..")` twice → drop `.named` (default names are unique) or add a counter |
| `sortie::session_ended` | the session ended before the command completed | normal at the end of a turn → return `Ok(())` |
| `sortie::unavailable` | the engine cannot run it now | no mission session is running; or a keyed command was in flight when the DCS link dropped ("whether it ran is not known": check the world, then use a new key) |
| `sortie::paused` | the simulation is paused | the command was sent with `.on_pause(v1::PausePolicy::Fail)` |
| `sortie::rejected` | the engine refused the command | read the message |
| `sortie::quarantined` | this command kind is disabled after it faulted the bridge | run `sortie doctor`, report it with `Logs/sortie-bridge.log` |
| `sortie::bridge_fault` | the bridge caught a fault | report it with `Logs/sortie-bridge.log` |
| `sortie::conflict` | a state write lost against another writer | `StateDoc::update` retries by itself; seen only after 8 conflicts in a row |

## Lookup and state errors

| Code | Message | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sortie::unknown_symbol` | "the running mission has no group `X`; regenerate the scenario lock" | the mission in DCS was built from another lock: `python scenario.py lock`, `cargo build`, register and launch the mission again |
| `sortie::not_in_world` | "group `X` is not in the world right now" | late activation, or all its units are dead → check `w.group(&groups::X).alive_count()` first, or match the error |
| `sortie::state` | "state `name`: ..." | the engine's store refused: read the message; a `T` that no longer deserializes the stored JSON (changed field types) also lands here: add `#[serde(default)]` to new fields |
| `sortie::transport` | "engine connection: ..." | the engine is unreachable: start `sortied`, check `--engine` / `SORTIE_ENGINE` |

## Build errors

| Where | Message (start) | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build.rs` | `error: sortie-build failed for scenario "x": <path>: ...` + `help: the path is relative to the logic crate's Cargo.toml; ...` | the lock path is wrong or the lock is missing: `python scenario.py lock` |
| `build.rs` | `... is for scenario "a", but build.rs asked for "b"` | the first argument of `sortie_build::scenario(..)` must be the lock's scenario name |
| `build.rs` | `help: the lock was edited by hand or is corrupt; ...` | regenerate the lock; never edit it |
| `include_scenario!` | `OUT_DIR is not set, so there is no generated scenario module to include` | add `sortie-build` to `[build-dependencies]` and the one-line `build.rs` |
| `include_scenario!` | ``no generated module for scenario `x` (...); build.rs generated: ...`` | use the same name in `include_scenario!` and `sortie_build::scenario` |
| `#[sortie::mission]` | ``a mission must be an `async fn` ...``, `the arguments are swapped ...`, ``a mission must return `sortie::Result<()>` ...`` | the signature is `async fn run(ctx: Ctx<M>, start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()>` |
| `#[sortie::mission]` | `` `X` is not a scenario marker `` | `Ctx<M>` takes the marker from the generated module, e.g. `Ctx<frontline::Frontline>` |
| `#[sortie::test]` | a compile error: tests without DCS arrive in SDK 0.2 | test decisions in plain functions with `#[test]`; test the mission in DCS |
| any `.await` on a borrow | clippy `await_holding_refcell_ref` | end the `ctx.world()` / `StateDoc::get()` borrow before the `.await` |

## Attach and runtime messages (the logic's stderr)

| Message | Meaning → fix |
| --- | --- |
| ``cannot reach the engine at http://127.0.0.1:50777: ... (is `sortied` running?); retrying in N s`` | start `sortied`; the logic keeps retrying (1 to 30 s) |
| ``error[sortie::transport]: Logic.Attach at ... failed: ... (set SORTIE_TOKEN to a token with the `logic` role)`` | exit code 2: set `SORTIE_TOKEN` (from `Saved Games\DCS\Sortie\tokens.toml`), or run `sortied --dev` locally |
| ``error[sortie::rejected]: the engine rejected this logic: logic `x` was built against a different `s` schema: N symbol(s) missing from the running mission`` + `missing symbols: ...` | exit code 2: the mission in DCS lacks symbols this logic was built with; build the logic and the mission from the same lock |
| ``another PRIMARY logic is attached for `s` `` | a second copy of the logic is running: stop the old process |
| ``a `observer` token cannot attach a logic (needs `logic` or `admin`)`` | use a `logic` token |
| `` `spawn_group` without `.key(..)` in dev mode: a hot reload would run it again; add a key such as `.key("spawn-group-1")` `` | the logic runs with `--dev`: add a key |
| ``in dev mode spawn_group and destroy need `.key(..)` (hot reload replays commands by key)`` | `sortied --dev` refused it: add a key |
| ``tick N: the world replica is borrowed across an `.await` ...`` | a `ctx.world()` guard lives across `.await`: shorten the borrow |
| `event stream lagged` (warning, `skipped = N`) | an event loop is too slow: keep it short, move slow work to another task |
| `task spawned at src/lib.rs:L:C returned` + report, or `... panicked at ...` | that task ended with an error; the others keep running |

<!-- source: agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/patterns.md -->

# Patterns for a long multiplayer mission (for agents)

A server mission runs for hours, holds thousands of units, and players come and go. The
patterns below keep it cheap and replay-safe. They use the `frontline` scenario.

## Shape: one task per concern

```rust
use sortie::prelude::*;
use sortie::proto::v1;
use sortie::types::Eid;

use frontline::{Frontline, airbases, groups, menus, templates, zones};

#[sortie::mission]
pub async fn run(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, _start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    // One task per concern; each lives until the session ends.
    ctx.spawn(support_menu);
    ctx.spawn(players);
    ctx.spawn(red_waves);
    ctx.spawn(front_control);
    ctx.spawn(idle_end);

    // The turn ends when the objective falls; otherwise the manifest's time limit ends it.
    ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count() == 0)
        .await;
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::BlueWin)
        .text("SAM North destroyed")
        .await
}
```

- Each concern (menus, players, AI waves, zone control, the idle timeout) is a plain
  `async fn name(ctx: Ctx<M>) -> sortie::Result<()>` started with `ctx.spawn(name)`. An error
  in one is recorded and ends only that task.
- The mission function itself waits for the end condition and calls `end_session`. Without
  one, the time limit of the scenario (`time_limit=` in `scenario.py`) ends the turn.
- Every task is a replayable script: after a logic restart all of them start again from the
  top, so each step is keyed, `once`d, timed by a named timer or a wait on world state.

## Players joining and leaving

```rust
/// Players joining and leaving: one loop over the raw event stream.
pub async fn players(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let mut events = ctx.events();
    while let Some(ev) = events.next().await {
        match ev.kind {
            Some(v1::event::Kind::PlayerEnteredUnit(e)) => {
                let Some(unit) = e.unit else { continue };
                let group = AnyGroup {
                    eid: unit.group_eid.and_then(Eid::from_u64),
                    name: unit.group_name,
                };
                let text = format!("Welcome, {}. F10 > Support has smoke.", e.player);
                match ctx.message(group).text(text).secs(15).await {
                    // Gone: the player left the slot before the message went out.
                    Ok(()) | Err(sortie::Error::Gone(_)) => {}
                    Err(err) => return Err(err),
                }
            }
            Some(v1::event::Kind::PlayerDisconnected(e)) => {
                eprintln!("{} left", e.name); // the logic's stderr
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- `PlayerEnteredUnit` comes for every player who takes a slot, also on a respawn into a new
  aircraft. `PlayerConnected` and `PlayerDisconnected` (player id, name, `ucid`) and
  `PlayerChangedSlot` (player id, name, coalition, slot) come from the server.
- Who is flying now is world state: `w.players()` (units with a player), `.coalition(..)`,
  `entity.player`. After a logic restart the event history is gone; the world is not.
- Per-group menus (`.per_group()`) reach groups that spawn later on their own: no code per
  join.
- Event-driven messages need no key: a replay does not see old events, so it cannot repeat
  them.

## AI waves

```rust
/// AI pressure: paced by named timers, keyed per wave, capped, scaled to the players online.
pub async fn red_waves(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let mut alive: Vec<Group<Air>> = Vec::new();
    for n in 1u32.. {
        ctx.timer(&format!("wave-{n}"), mins(15)).await;
        alive.retain(Group::is_alive);
        let blue = ctx.world().players().coalition(Coalition::Blue).count();
        if blue == 0 || alive.len() >= 4 {
            continue; // nobody to fight, or enough red in the air already
        }
        let cap = ctx
            .spawn_group(templates::RED_CAP)
            .from_airbase(airbases::MAYKOP, StartType::Hot)
            .key(format!("wave-{n}"))
            .await?;
        cap.push_task(Task::cap(zones::FRONT))
            .key(format!("wave-{n}-task"))
            .await?;
        alive.push(cap);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- A named timer per wave paces the loop and survives a logic restart; a key per wave makes the
  spawn and its task happen once.
- The decision (players online, red already in the air) reads the world as it is now. A replay
  decides again only for waves that never spawned.
- Cap the number of live AI groups. The engine paces spawns (currently 2 groups or 24 units a
  second) and a spawn waits at most 30 s by default: a wave of many groups is a loop of
  awaited spawns, not hundreds of commands at once.
- A spawned group's name is `<template name>#<session4>-<n>`; find spawned groups in queries by
  their `Group` handle, not by name.

## Thousands of units

- `wait_until` runs its predicate after every tick (10 a second) and every event. A predicate
  over a group (`w.group(&g).alive_count()`) or a zone (`.any_inside(zone)`, indexed by a
  spatial grid) is cheap. A predicate that scans every unit is not: poll it every few seconds
  with `ctx.sleep` instead.

```rust
/// A periodic check instead of `wait_until`: cheap with thousands of units.
pub async fn front_control(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    loop {
        ctx.sleep(secs(30)).await;
        let (red, blue) = {
            let w = ctx.world();
            let red = w
                .units()
                .coalition(Coalition::Red)
                .ground()
                .count_inside(zones::FRONT);
            let blue = w
                .units()
                .coalition(Coalition::Blue)
                .ground()
                .count_inside(zones::FRONT);
            (red, blue)
        }; // the borrow of the world ends here, before the next .await
        if red == 0 && blue > 0 {
            ctx.message(sortie::MessageTarget::All)
                .text("Blue holds the front")
                .key("front-taken")
                .await?;
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
}
```

- Symbols are for what the logic names. Ten scenario groups with idents and hundreds of
  anonymous ones (from templates or a `@sc.pydcs` hook) is normal: query those by zone, type
  (`.of_type(..)`), coalition, or DCS name (`.in_group("Name")`).
- An event stream that falls more than 1024 events behind drops the oldest. Keep each event
  loop short; hand slow work (spawns, many messages) to another task. Several typed streams
  (`.of::<v1::Dead>()`, `.of::<v1::Kill>()`) are cheaper to keep up than one loop that awaits
  inside.
- Read the world in a block and drop the borrow before the next `.await`.

## Idle server

```rust
/// Ends the turn after 30 minutes of model time without a player in a slot.
pub async fn idle_end(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let mut idle_minutes = 0;
    loop {
        ctx.sleep(mins(1)).await;
        let online = ctx.world().players().count();
        idle_minutes = if online == 0 { idle_minutes + 1 } else { 0 };
        if idle_minutes == 30 {
            return ctx
                .end_session(Outcome::Aborted)
                .text("No players for 30 minutes")
                .await;
        }
    }
}
```

Model time stops while the simulation is paused; a server that pauses without players never
reaches the 30 minutes, which is what you want.

## Scores and other campaign data

```rust
/// Campaign-wide scores, kept by the engine.
#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Scores {
    pub kills: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u32>,
}

pub async fn scores(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let scores = ctx.state::<Scores>("scores").await?;
    let mut kills = ctx.events().of::<v1::Kill>().coalition(Coalition::Blue);
    while let Some(kill) = kills.next().await {
        let Some(player) = kill.initiator.and_then(|u| u.player) else {
            continue; // an AI kill
        };
        scores
            .update(|s| *s.kills.entry(player.clone()).or_default() += 1)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- Campaign documents live in the engine and survive restarts of the logic, the mission and the
  engine; the generator reads them for the next turn.
- Every `update` is a round trip to the engine. One per kill is fine; for high-rate data
  (hits, shots) count locally and write once a minute.
- A logic restart does not replay old events, so an event-driven counter never counts twice.
  A counter driven by a replayed step (a wave, an objective) goes inside `ctx.once_per_turn`.

## Instead of → do

| Instead of | Do |
| --- | --- |
| a spawn or destroy without a key | `.key("step-name")` on every spawn and destroy |
| a key built from model time, a random number or an Eid | a key built from the step: a literal or a deterministic counter |
| the same key with a changing text | a key per distinct command, or no key for event-driven messages |
| `ctx.sleep` for a delay that must survive a restart | `ctx.timer("name", dur)` |
| waiting for a `Dead` event | a `wait_until` on `w.group(&g).alive_count() == 0` |
| `campaign.update(..)` in the open | inside `ctx.once_per_turn(..)` |
| holding `ctx.world()` or `doc.get()` across `.await` | a block that ends before the `.await` |
| `std::thread::sleep`, blocking I/O, `std::thread::spawn` | `ctx.sleep`, `ctx.spawn` |
| hundreds of spawns at once | a loop of awaited spawns with a cap |
| a `wait_until` predicate scanning every unit | a group or zone predicate, or a poll with `ctx.sleep` |
| `ctx.group(groups::X)?` on a group that may be dead | match `Error::NotInWorld`, or check `alive_count()` first |
| `.unwrap()` on command results | `?`, or a `match` on the errors the step expects (`Gone`, `SessionEnded`) |
| editing `scenario.lock.json` | `python scenario.py lock` |

<!-- source: agents/sortie-scenario/SKILL.md -->

Skill `sortie-scenario` (sortie-scenario/SKILL.md): Sortie scenarios in Python (`scenario.py` with sortie-gen over pydcs, DCS World). Use when writing or changing a scenario (zones, ground groups, air templates, statics or other pydcs content, airbases, player flights and their airfield coalition, flags, F10 menus), when running `lock`, `build`, `validate`, `register`, `launch`, `restart`, `watch` or `results`, when a sortie-gen error or warning appears, or when the Rust logic needs a new symbol.


# Sortie scenarios

`scenario.py` declares the static part of a mission. sortie-gen (a wrapper over pydcs 1.0.0)
builds three things from it:

- the `.miz`, with one MISSION START trigger whose DO SCRIPT calls `SORTIE.attach{..}`;
- the manifest (`<build_id>.manifest.pb` and `.json`): groups, units, zones, templates, flags,
  airbases, menus, player slots, as the engine and the logic see them;
- `scenario.lock.json`: the symbols (idents) the Rust logic compiles against. It is the
  contract between the two sides: commit it, never edit it.

An `ident=` makes a symbol: `groups::SAM_NORTH`, `zones::FRONT`, `templates::RED_CAP`,
`airbases::MAYKOP`, `flags::SAM_DOWN`, `menus::SITREP` in Rust. Without an ident a zone is
only in the `.miz`, and a group is in the `.miz` and the manifest but has no Rust symbol.

## Setup

```powershell
uv add "sortie-gen @ git+https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk@v0.1.0#subdirectory=python/sortie-gen"
```

Or install the `sortie_gen` wheel from the GitHub release. Python 3.11+.

## A scenario, step by step

The `frontline` scenario that the mission-logic skill uses. Header: name, schema, map, start,
time limit.

```python
from dcs import planes, statics, vehicles
from dcs.terrain import caucasus

from sortie_gen import Coalition, Scenario, StartType

sc = Scenario(
    "frontline",
    schema=1,
    theatre=caucasus.Caucasus(),
    start="2026-11-01T07:00:00Z",  # RFC 3339; without an offset: the map's local time
    time_limit="4h",  # the engine ends the session (turn) after 4 h of model time
)
```

Zones: a circle (`at` + `radius`, metres) or a quad (`points=[4 points]`).

```python
obj = sc.zone("Objective", ident="OBJECTIVE", at=sc.latlon(44.62, 40.10), radius=500)
ring = sc.zone("SAM Ring", ident="SAM_RING", at=obj.center, radius=60_000)
front = sc.zone("Front", ident="FRONT", at=sc.latlon(44.95, 38.60), radius=20_000)
sc.zone("Editor note", at=sc.latlon(44.70, 40.00), radius=1_000)  # no ident: .miz only
```

Ground groups are placed in the `.miz`; unit `k` is named `<group>-<k>`.

```python
sc.ground_group(
    "SAM North",
    ident="SAM_NORTH",
    country="Russia",
    at=obj.center,
    units=[
        vehicles.AirDefence.S_300PS_54K6_cp,
        vehicles.AirDefence.S_300PS_40B6M_tr,
        vehicles.AirDefence.S_300PS_64H6E_sr,
        *[vehicles.AirDefence.S_300PS_5P85C_ln] * 4,
    ],
    roles={"sam", "north"},
)
sc.ground_group(
    "Red Armor",
    ident="RED_ARMOR",
    country="Russia",
    at=front.center,
    units=[vehicles.Armor.T_72B] * 4,
    formation="line",
    heading=270,
    roles={"armor"},
)
```

Air templates stay out of the `.miz`: the logic spawns them (`ctx.spawn_group`).

```python
sc.air_template(
    "Red CAP",
    planes.Su_27,
    ident="RED_CAP",
    country="Russia",
    size=2,
    airbase="Maykop-Khanskaya",  # default placement when the logic gives none
    payload=[  # pylon tuples: the hermetic build knows no default loadout for this task
        planes.Su_27.Pylon1.R_73__AA_11_Archer____Infra_Red,
        planes.Su_27.Pylon10.R_73__AA_11_Archer____Infra_Red,
    ],
)
```

Airbases (symbols for the logic) and player slots:

```python
sc.airbase("Maykop-Khanskaya", ident="MAYKOP", coalition=Coalition.Red)
sc.airbase("Krymsk", ident="KRYMSK")  # the player flights below give it to blue
sc.player_flight(
    "Viper 1", planes.F_16C_50, country="USA", airbase="Krymsk", start=StartType.Cold, size=2
)
sc.player_flight(
    "Hog 1", planes.A_10C_2, country="USA", airbase="Krymsk", start=StartType.Hot, size=2
)
```

Flags and F10 menu commands (the logic installs the menus):

```python
sc.flag("SAM_DOWN")
sc.menu("SMOKE_OBJECTIVE", "Smoke the objective", path=["Support"])
sc.menu("SITREP", "Situation report")
```

Everything Sortie does not wrap (statics, air groups placed in the `.miz`, weather, briefing,
your own triggers) goes in a `@sc.pydcs` hook. It runs on every build after the declarations.
Groups it adds are in the manifest without an ident; reach them by DCS name.

```python
from dcs.triggers import TriggerStart

from sortie_gen.miz import InlineDoScript


@sc.pydcs
def extras(m):
    # What Sortie does not wrap: statics, weather, briefing, your own triggers.
    hq = sc.latlon(44.61, 40.08)
    m.static_group(m.country("Russia"), "Red HQ", statics.Fortification._Command_Center, hq)
    t = TriggerStart(comment="welcome")
    t.add_action(InlineDoScript('trigger.action.outText("Frontline is live", 15)'))
    m.triggerrules.triggers.append(t)
```

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sc.cli()  # lock | build | validate | register | launch | restart | watch | results
```

All signatures and defaults: [references/reference.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-scenario/references/reference.md).

## Rules

1. **Positions** are `sc.latlon(lat, lon)`, `sc.point(north, east)` (editor axes, metres), a
   zone (`zone.center` or the handle) or an airbase handle. A bare tuple is refused.
2. **Names.** DCS group names are unique across groups, templates and player flights, at most
   128 bytes, without `#` (reserved for spawned groups: `<template>#<session4>-<n>`). Idents
   match `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` and are unique per kind; roles `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`; the scenario name
   `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` and not a Rust keyword. sortie-gen refuses a bad name at the declaration.
3. **The airfield coalition rule (multiplayer).** DCS offers a parking slot only to the
   coalition that owns the airfield; at a neutral or enemy airfield the player stays a
   spectator. So `player_flight` with a `Cold`, `Hot` or `Runway` start gives its airfield to
   the flight's coalition. The build fails when the scenario gives that airbase to another
   coalition (`airbase(.., coalition=..)`) or starts flights of two coalitions there. A client
   group added by a `@sc.pydcs` hook gets only a warning: fix its airfield owner in the hook.
4. **Late activation** (`late_activation=True`) has no activate command in the SDK: a group
   that appears later is an `air_template` the logic spawns.
5. **A symbol change needs both sides.** Add or rename an ident → `lock` → `cargo build` of
   the logic → `register` a new build. Moving a zone or a unit changes no symbol: the logic
   needs no change (the running manifest's geometry wins).

## Commands

Run from the mission repository: `uv run python scenario.py <command>`.

| Command | Does | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lock [--check]` | writes `scenario.lock.json`; `--check` only fails if it is stale (CI) | nothing |
| `build [--out DIR] [--no-miz] [--stem NAME] [--locked]` | offline build into `dist/` (or `--out`); updates the lock unless `--locked` | nothing |
| `validate` | asks DCS whether it knows every unit and static type | a running mission with Sortie (the lobby is enough) |
| `register [--out DIR] [--no-validate]` | engine build id, build, type check, `Missions.Register`; the engine stores the `.miz` in `Saved Games\DCS\Missions\Sortie\` | `sortied` |
| `launch [--build-id ID] [--no-validate]` | registers a fresh build (without `--build-id`) and loads it in DCS | a dedicated server with Sortie |
| `restart` | reloads the running mission: its session ends (reason `restart`), a new one starts with `Start::Restart` | a multiplayer server or host; single player refuses at once |
| `watch [--kinds dead,birth] [--from-seq N] [--session S]` | engine health and the live event stream | `sortied` |
| `results [--session S] [--json]` | results of the last (or a given) session: outcome, fates, kills, flags, report | `sortied` |

The engine address is `--engine`, `SORTIE_ENGINE` or `127.0.0.1:50777`; the token is
`--token` or `SORTIE_TOKEN` (role `generator`; not needed with `sortied --dev`). Exit codes: 0
done, 1 error, 2 a feature that is not built yet.

Single player: `launch` needs a server, so `register`, then open
`Saved Games\DCS\Missions\Sortie\<scenario>-<build_id>.miz` in DCS yourself.

## Builds and turns

- **Determinism.** An offline `build` derives the build id from the content (start time,
  manifest, mission): the same scenario gives byte-identical files on one machine; the manifest
  and the lock are meant to match across machines too. By default the build uses only the data
  inside pydcs (hermetic): a template without a default loadout warns "spawns without weapons";
  pass `payload=` (pylon tuples, as above). `SORTIE_GEN_DCS_DATA=installed` uses the installed
  DCS loadouts and makes the build machine-dependent.
- **A build is a turn.** `register` takes a fresh build id from the engine every time, so a new
  registration starts a new turn: `Start::Fresh`, fresh keys, `once` and `once_per_turn`.
  `restart` keeps the build (same turn).
- **Type check.** `register` and `launch` stop when DCS on the server does not know a type
  (a typo, a missing module or mod) and print where it is used. When the check cannot run (no
  mission, the server is paused, an older engine) they warn and register anyway.
  `--no-validate` skips it.

## The Mission Editor and DO SCRIPT

- A built `.miz` can be opened, re-saved and flown from the Mission Editor: the bootstrap is
  stored the way the editor writes DO SCRIPT (code inline in the action), so the mission still
  attaches.
- Change groups, units and zones in `scenario.py`, not in the editor: the manifest describes
  the build, and an edited `.miz` no longer matches it.
- A DO SCRIPT added in a `@sc.pydcs` hook uses `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`, not pydcs's
  `DoScript` (the editor would run its dictionary key as Lua).
- Do not load and save a built `.miz` with pydcs: it rewrites every DO SCRIPT into the
  dictionary form.
- `uv run sortie-gen adopt my.miz [--json]` lists the coalitions, groups, units and zones of an
  editor mission with proposed idents: the start for porting it to `scenario.py`.

## More

- [references/reference.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-scenario/references/reference.md): every declaration with its parameters,
  the CLI flags, the `sortie-gen` command, and the generator's errors.
- The Rust side: the sortie-mission-logic skill. Running in DCS: the sortie-live-debugging
  skill. Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-scenario/references/reference.md -->

# sortie-gen reference (for agents)

`from sortie_gen import Scenario, StartType, Coalition`. Unit and aircraft types are pydcs
classes (`dcs.vehicles.*`, `dcs.planes.*`, `dcs.helicopters.*`); countries are pydcs country
names (`"Russia"`, `"USA"`); airbases are names of the map's airports (`"Krymsk"`) or
`sc.theatre.airports[..]`. Unknown names fail with a "did you mean" hint.

## Declarations

| Declaration | Parameters (defaults) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Scenario(name, *, schema, theatre, start, time_limit=None, description=None)` | `name`: `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`; `schema`: int ≥ 1; `theatre`: a pydcs terrain (`caucasus.Caucasus()`); `start`: RFC 3339, without an offset the map's local time; `time_limit`: `"3h"`, `"1h30m"`, `"90m"`, seconds, `None` = no limit | the scenario |
| `sc.zone(name, *, ident=None, at=, radius=)` or `points=[p1, p2, p3, p4]`; `hidden=True`, `color=None` | a circle or a quad | `ZoneHandle` (`.center`) |
| `sc.ground_group(name, *, ident=None, country, at, units=[..], heading=0.0, formation="star", spacing=40.0, skill="Excellent", roles=None, late_activation=False, hidden=False)` | `formation`: `line`, `star`, `rectangle`, `vee`; the first unit stands at `at`; units named `<name>-<k>` | `GroupHandle` |
| `sc.air_template(name, unit_type, *, ident, country, size=1, task=None, at=None, airbase=None, altitude=None, speed=None, skill="High", roles=None, payload=None)` | kept out of the `.miz`; `task` defaults to the type's main task; placement when the logic gives none: `at`, else `airbase`, else the first declared airbase, else the coalition's bullseye; `altitude` 6000 m (2000 m for helicopters); `speed` in km/h; `payload`: a pydcs loadout name or a list of pylon tuples | `TemplateHandle` |
| `sc.airbase(name, *, ident, coalition=None)` | `coalition`: `Coalition.Red/Blue/Neutral` or `"red"`; without it the map's default owner stays (except player airfields) | `AirbaseHandle` (`.position`) |
| `sc.player_flight(name, unit_type, *, country, airbase, start=StartType.Cold, size=1, task=None, skill="Client", payload=None, at=None, altitude=3000.0)` | `start`: `StartType.Cold`, `Hot`, `Runway`, `Air` (`Air` needs `at=`); the type must be flyable; goes to `manifest.player_flights`, not to the lock | `FlightHandle` |
| `sc.flag(ident, *, name=None, initial=0)` | DCS flag name defaults to the ident; a non-zero `initial` is set by a MISSION START trigger | `FlagHandle` |
| `sc.menu(ident, label, *, path=())` | `path`: sub-menus, e.g. `["Support"]` | `MenuHandle` |
| `@sc.pydcs` on `def hook(mission)` | runs after the declarations on every build; names are checked for uniqueness afterwards | the function |
| `sc.latlon(lat, lon)`, `sc.point(north, east)` | positions; `latlon` is rounded to 1 mm | `dcs.mapping.Point` |
| `sc.time_limit = "2h"` | changes the limit after construction | |
| `sc.build(build_id=None)` | in-memory build: `.build_id`, `.manifest`, `.miz`, `.lock`, `.warnings`, `.write(out_dir)` | `Build` |
| `sc.cli()` | the command line below | exits |

Idents are optional for zones and ground groups (no ident: no Rust symbol) and required for
templates, airbases, flags and menus.

## `python scenario.py` flags

```text
lock      [--out FILE] [--check]
build     [--out DIR] [--lock FILE] [--locked] [--build-id ULID] [--stem NAME] [--no-miz]
validate  [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
register  [--out DIR] [--lock FILE] [--locked] [--no-validate] [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
launch    [--build-id ID] [--out DIR] [--lock FILE] [--locked] [--no-validate] [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
restart   [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
watch     [--session S] [--kinds birth,dead,...] [--from-seq N] [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
results   [--session S] [--json] [--engine ADDR] [--token T] [--timeout S]
```

- `--timeout`: seconds per engine call (default 15).
- `watch --kinds`: `birth`, `dead`, `unit_lost`, `kill`, `hit`, `shot`, `takeoff`, `land`,
  `base_captured`, `mark`, `player_entered_unit`, `unit_gone`, `menu_pressed`,
  `player_connected`, `player_disconnected`, `player_changed_slot`, `chat_message`,
  `simulation_paused`, `simulation_resumed`, `gap`, `unknown`.
- `build --no-miz --stem NAME --out DIR` writes only the manifest files.
- `launch --build-id ID` builds and checks nothing: it loads a build registered earlier.

## `sortie-gen`

```text
sortie-gen lock|build|validate|register|launch <scenario.py> [flags]
sortie-gen restart|watch|results [flags]                 # no scenario file needed
sortie-gen lobby [--out missions/sortie-lobby.miz] [--theatre caucasus]
sortie-gen adopt my.miz [--json]
```

- `lobby` writes the idle mission for a dedicated server's `missionList` (no units, no
  bootstrap; it shows whether the bridge loaded). The engine uses the running lobby to check
  types.
- `adopt` reports an editor mission: groups, units, zones, proposed idents, names that break
  the rules. pydcs may move aircraft to other parking spots when it saves a mission: place
  player slots with `player_flight`.
- `worker` (the campaign loop) is not available yet: it exits with code 2.

## Errors and warnings

The CLI prints `error: ...` without a traceback. In code they are `sortie_gen` exceptions:
`InvalidName`, `NameConflict`, `ScenarioError`, `LockError`, `UnknownTypes`, `EngineError`,
`EngineUnavailable`, `EngineNotReady`, `NotYet` (all `GeneratorError`).

| Message (start) | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `... ident 'x' must match [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` | idents are Rust constants: `SAM_NORTH` |
| `a group named 'X' already exists in this scenario` / `two groups are named 'X'` | DCS would destroy one of them: rename |
| `... contains '#', which is reserved for spawned groups` | drop the `#` |
| `pass a position made with sc.latlon(lat, lon), sc.point(north, east), a zone or an airbase` | a bare tuple is ambiguous |
| `player flights 'A' (blue) and 'B' (red) both start at X` | one airfield, one coalition: move a flight or use an air start |
| `player flight 'A' (blue) starts at X, which the scenario gives to red` | give the airbase to the flight's coalition or start elsewhere |
| warning `player group 'A' (blue) starts at X, which belongs to red` | a hook placed a client group: set the airfield owner in the hook |
| warning `template 'X' (Su-27) spawns without weapons` | `payload=[..]` pylon tuples, or `SORTIE_GEN_DCS_DATA=installed` |
| `pydcs knows no loadout 'X' for Y` | a loadout name needs `SORTIE_GEN_DCS_DATA=installed`; or list the pylons |
| `scenario.lock.json is stale (...); run python scenario.py lock` | after `--locked` / `--check`: run `lock`, rebuild the logic |
| warning `the symbol set changed: rebuild the mission logic (cargo build)` | rebuild the logic before running it against the new build |
| `DCS on the server does not know N type(s) this scenario uses:` | fix the type name, or install the module or mod on the server; `--no-validate` skips the check |
| warning `unit and static types not checked: ... (registering anyway)` | no mission ran in DCS, or it was paused; start the lobby to get the check |
| `cannot reach the Sortie engine at 127.0.0.1:50777 (...). Is sortied running?` | start `sortied --dev` locally, or point `--engine` / `SORTIE_ENGINE` at it |
| `... FAILED_PRECONDITION ...` on `restart` | single player, or the hooks part of Sortie predates the install: restart DCS itself |
